result:
A component re-renders only when its own state changes, its parent re-renders, or a context it reads changes, so the fix depends on which of those is firing. React DevTools Profiler with "Record why each component rendered" enabled will tell you.

The most common cause is a parent re-rendering, which re-renders every child regardless of whether props changed. Fix it by wrapping the child in `React.memo`, or better, by moving the changing state down into the component that actually uses it so that the expensive child sits outside the re-rendering subtree (passing it as `children` also works).

If `React.memo` is already there and it still re-renders, the props are new references each time: inline objects, arrays, or arrow functions like `style={{...}}` or `onClick={() => ...}`. Hoist constants out of the component, and wrap the rest in `useMemo` and `useCallback` with correct dependencies.

Context is the next culprit: every consumer re-renders when the provider's `value` changes, and `value={{ user, setUser }}` is a new object on every render. Memoize the value with `useMemo`, and split a context that mixes fast-changing and slow-changing data into two.

With a store such as Redux or Zustand, a selector that returns a fresh object or array (`state => ({ a: state.a, b: state.b })`) triggers a render on every store update. Select primitives separately, or pass a shallow equality function.

An effect that sets state on every run causes an extra render each cycle, usually because of a missing or unstable dependency array, or because it is syncing state that could be computed. Compute derived values during render instead of storing them, and fix the dependencies.

Two things look like extra renders but are not. Unstable keys (`key={Math.random()}`, or an index on a reordering list) remount the component entirely, so use stable IDs. StrictMode deliberately double-invokes renders in development only, and needs no fix.
